notes: source.string.v1 with card CT07-SLICE-PERMISSIONS's range-wise borrow_utf8(NAME, LOW, HIGH). Two loans of [0, 2) and [4, 6) of one six-byte buffer are live at the same time while the owner writes bytes 2 and 3 between them; the writes are admitted because disjointness is decided at check time (max low < min high, exact because every bound is a check-time constant), and a third view then reads the written bytes back so the admission is visible in the observation. BOUNDARY, stated as the semantic profile states it: one of the two disjoint permissions is a READ loan and the other is the owner's retained write authority - this is disjoint permission over two ranges, not two parties each holding write authority (that lend is unlanded residual SLICE-PERMISSIONS-WRITE-LEND). The bounds half is the out_of_extent control's Q077 refusal; the disjointness half is the overlapping control's Q078 refusal, which is CT08's own case shape.

controls.note: Disjointness: the identical program with one byte of the write moved inside head's [0, 2). Refused naming the footprint, so the case's admission is a decided disjointness rather than a route that admits owner writes anywhere. This program is CT08's own case.

Bounds: the identical program with one byte of the write moved past the declared extent. Refused at check time by source.buffer.v1's own bounds rule, reported at Q077 on this composed route - a refusal, not a run-time trap.
